title: NEB Class 11 Biology — Ecology — 2022
subject: biology
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: What is ecological succession? Explain with the example of xerosere.
questions.solution:
**Ecological succession:** Gradual change in species composition of a community over time.

**Xerosere** (dry habitat succession):
Lichen → Moss → Herbaceous plants → Shrub → Forest

Pioneer species (lichens) colonize bare rock, weather it, build soil, allowing larger plants to establish.
questions.knowledgeNote: Climax community = stable end stage. Hydrosere = succession in water.
questions.answer: **Ecological succession:** the **orderly, directional and predictable change in the structure and species composition of a community over time**, beginning from a bare or disturbed area and progressing through a series of stages (**seres**) toward a relatively stable **climax community** — driven by the community itself modifying the environment (soil build-up, shade, moisture) until a new set of species can take over. **Xerosere (succession on dry bare rock):** **(1) Crustose lichen stage:** lichens colonise bare rock, etching it with acids — the pioneer community; dead lichen matter forms the first soil film. **(2) Foliose lichen stage:** leafy lichens replace crustose ones, trapping more dust and building more humus. **(3) Moss stage:** with enough substrate, mosses establish, deepening the soil and holding moisture. **(4) Herbaceous stage:** grasses and herbs (the 'higher' plants) oust the mosses; soil deepens further. **(5) Shrub stage:** shrubs (e.g. *Rhus*, *Ziziphus*) invade, shading out herbs. **(6) Climax forest:** ultimately trees establish — in the moist tropics a broad-leaved climax forest — the stable endpoint whose composition is self-perpetuating. **Deep point:** succession is the ecosystem building its own ground floor — each stage makes the site more hospitable and thereby signs its own replacement; the climax is not the best community, just the one that can hold the ground it stands on.

questions.question: A grassland ecosystem has a gross primary productivity of 4800 kcal m^-2 yr^-1 and plant respiration of 1200 kcal m^-2 yr^-1. (a) Calculate the net primary productivity. (b) If herbivore respiration is 400 kcal m^-2 yr^-1 and all the NPP is consumed by herbivores, how much energy is passed to the next trophic level as secondary production?
questions.solution:
**Given:** GPP = 4800 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹; respiration of plants (R) = 1200 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹; respiration of herbivores (R₂) = 400 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹.

**Step 1 — Net primary productivity (NPP)**

NPP is the amount of food energy actually stored as plant biomass after the plants have used some of the GPP for their own respiration.

$$\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - R = 4800 - 1200 = 3600\ \text{kcal m}^{-2}\ \text{yr}^{-1}$$

**Step 2 — Secondary production of herbivores**

The energy that herbivores store as their own body tissue (secondary production) is what they ingest minus what they burn in respiration.

$$\text{Secondary production} = \text{NPP} - R_2 = 3600 - 400 = 3200\ \text{kcal m}^{-2}\ \text{yr}^{-1}$$

$$\text{Energy passed to carnivores} = 3200\ \text{kcal m}^{-2}\ \text{yr}^{-1}$$

**Interpretations:**
- The plants of this grassland keep 3600 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹ (75% of GPP) as net biomass; **primary productivity = NPP**, not GPP.
- The value is high here only because *all* the NPP was assumed to be eaten. In a natural ecosystem only about **10%** of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next (**Lindeman's ten percent rule**), because most is lost as respiration, heat, excretion and to decomposers.
questions.knowledgeNote: NPP equals GPP minus plant respiration, and by the ten percent rule only about a tenth of energy passes to the next trophic level.
questions.answer: **(a) Net Primary Productivity:** NPP = GPP − R (plant respiration) = 4800 − 1200 = **3600 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹**. **(b) NPP is the energy actually stored in plant tissue** — the food available to the next trophic level (herbivores and decomposers). Only about **10%** of it passes to the herbivore level by the ten-percent law, so the herbivore level can expect roughly 360 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹ and the carnivore level ~36 kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹. **Deep point:** GPP is the plant's gross salary, R its living expenses, NPP its savings — and the rest of the food chain lives entirely off the savings.
